item.title: TwinIR: Coordinated Invisible Dual-Point Attacks on Online HD Map Construction
item.summary: arXiv:2608.04453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Online HD map construction is critical to prediction and planning in autonomous driving. We find that existing physical attacks against online map construction are limited by a cross-boundary compensation effect: after the target boundary is perturbed, another visible boundary may retain sufficient geometric cues for the model to recover the original road geometry. Based on this observation, we propose TwinIR, a new mechanism-guided physical attack methodology for online map construction. TwinIR jointly optimizes attack effectiveness and point sparsity, seeking the minimum number of attack points needed to suppress compensating geometric cues from surrounding boundaries. To reduce the perceptibility of multi-point attacks, TwinIR models camera responses to near-infrared illumination and maps optimized attack points to feasible physical placements, producing camera-visible interference with minimal visible-spectrum changes.
